title: Application of derivative in road taxation
competency: Find a minimum cost or best design with derivatives.

keywords.def: Finding the input that gives the largest or smallest value of a quantity.

en.text: Write the quantity to make smallest or largest as a function of one variable (use the given constraint to remove the other variable). Differentiate, set the derivative to 0, reject impossible values like negative lengths, and check the sign change.

am.text: ትንሽ ወይም ትልቅ የምናደርገውን መጠን በአንድ ተለዋዋጭ እንጽፋለን፤ ዴሪቫቲቩን 0 እናደርጋለን፤ አሉታዊ ርዝመቶችን እንጥላለን።

screens.title: Driving more to pay less per mile?
screens.ask: A car has fixed yearly costs (tax, insurance) plus costs that grow with mileage. As yearly mileage grows, the average cost per mile
screens.after:
Fixed costs (160 birr) are shared over more miles: 160/x falls.
Depreciation 0.00001x² grows faster than x, so its share 0.00001x rises.
First the falling part wins, then the rising part.
So there is a best mileage where the cost per mile is least.

screens.title: Road taxation
paras: Tax 50 birr and insurance 110 birr a year. Petrol 0.75x/30, service 20x/3000, depreciation 0.00001x².
Average cost per mile M = C/x = 160/x + 0.025 + 0.0067 + 0.00001x.

screens.title: Average cost per mile
screens.ask: Move the yearly mileage x. Where is M smallest?
screens.note: The minimum is at 4000 miles (about 0.11 birr per mile).

screens.title: Key words
defs: Finding the input that gives the largest or smallest value of a quantity.

screens.ask: Best mileage: M′(x) = −160/x² + 0.00001 = 0. The mileage with the least cost per mile is x = ___ miles
screens.why:
Move the term: 0.00001 = 160/x².
x² = 160 ÷ 0.00001 = 16 000 000.
x = ±4000.
Mileage cannot be negative, so x = 4000 miles.
Check: M′ goes − to + at 4000, a minimum.

screens.title: Fence: try different shapes
screens.ask: Area 3200 ft². Sides x cost $1/ft (two of them), sides y cost $2/ft (two of them). Move x.
screens.note: The cost is lowest at x = 80, y = 40: $320. A square (x ≈ 56.6) costs more, about $339.

screens.title: Fence 3200 ft²: two sides cost $1/ft, two sides $2/ft

screens.text: Put the steps for solving an optimisation problem in order.
items: Write the quantity to make largest or smallest
Use the constraint to write it with one variable
Differentiate and set the derivative to 0
Reject impossible roots and check the sign change
screens.why:
1. Say what to optimise: cost, area, volume.
2. Use the given fact (area 3200, volume 128π) to remove one variable.
3. Differentiate and solve f′(x) = 0.
4. Throw away negative lengths, then check − to + (minimum) or + to − (maximum).
screens.clue: You need a function of ONE variable before you can differentiate.

screens.ask: Open box with a square base and surface area 48. The base side that gives the largest volume is ___
screens.why:
Base x by x, height h, no top: area x² + 4xh = 48.
So h = (48 − x²)/(4x).
V = x²h = (48x − x³)/4 = 12x − x³/4.
V′ = 12 − 3x²/4 = 0 gives x² = 16, x = 4 (reject −4).
Then h = 32/16 = 2. Answer: base side 4.

screens.ask: Closed can (cylinder) holding 128π cm³. The radius that uses the least material is ___ cm
screens.why:
Volume: πr²h = 128π, so h = 128/r².
Surface: S = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr² + 256π/r.
S′ = 4πr − 256π/r² = 0 gives r³ = 64.
r = 4 cm (and h = 8 cm).
Check: S′ goes − to +, a minimum. Note: h = 2r.

screens.text: True or false? In optimisation you keep every root of the derivative, even negative lengths.
screens.why:
Roots of the derivative are only candidates.
A length, a mileage or a number of items cannot be negative.
So x = −4000 miles is rejected.
False: keep only roots that make sense in the problem.

screens.ask: Largest product: two positive numbers add to 20. Their product is largest when the smaller number is ___
screens.why:
Let the numbers be x and 20 − x.
Product P = x(20 − x) = 20x − x².
P′ = 20 − 2x = 0 gives x = 10.
P′ goes + to −: a maximum. Both numbers are 10, product 100.
So the smaller number is 10 (they are equal).
screens.clue: Write the product with one variable.

items.text: Fencing 3200 ft²: two opposite sides cost $1/ft, the other two $2/ft. Pick the dimensions of least cost.
items.why:
Area: xy = 3200, so y = 3200/x.
Cost: C = 2x(1) + 2y(2) = 2x + 12 800/x.
C′ = 2 − 12 800/x² = 0 gives x² = 6400, x = 80.
y = 3200/80 = 40.
So 80 ft for the $1 sides, 40 ft for the $2 sides (cost $320).
Trap: 56.6 ft = √3200 is a square, best only if all sides cost the same.

items.ask: Open box with a square base, surface area 48: the largest volume is ___
Closed can holding 128π cm³: the height that uses the least material is ___ cm
items.why:
Least material at r = 4 cm.
h = 128/r² = 128/16.
h = 8 cm (the height equals the diameter).

test.ask: Minimum of a cost function: M(x) = 100/x + x/4 for x > 0. M is least at x = ___
test.why:
M′(x) = −100/x² + 1/4.
M′ = 0 gives x² = 400.
x = 20 (reject −20, since x > 0).
M′ goes − to +: a minimum, M(20) = 5 + 5 = 10.

test.ask: Largest area: a rectangle has perimeter 40 m. Its largest area is ___ m²

test.text: True or false? A cost function can have a minimum where its derivative is 0.
test.why:
At a minimum the tangent is flat, so the derivative is 0.
Check the sign: − before and + after.
Example: C(x) = x + 64/x has C′(8) = 0 and a minimum there.
True.

test.ask: Largest product: x + y = 12 with x, y > 0. The largest value of xy is ___
test.why:
y = 12 − x, so P = x(12 − x) = 12x − x².
P′ = 12 − 2x = 0 gives x = 6.
y = 6, so xy = 36.
Trap: 6 is x, not the product.

test.ask: Least cost: C(x) = x + 64/x for x > 0. The least cost is ___

notes.text: The road-tax example mixes birr and pence (100 pence = 1 birr) as the book does.
Exercise 2.20 (fencing, open box, can) uses dollars and units as printed.

screens.text: First derivative test: f′ changes from − to + at c. Then f(c) is a
screens.why:
f′ < 0 before c: the graph falls.
f′ > 0 after c: the graph rises.
Falling then rising makes a valley.
So f(c) is a relative minimum.
